# Adopt Context Docs

Apply the sibling [context-docs skill](../context-docs/SKILL.md)
to the current project and establish ongoing use. Read that skill first; it owns
the maintenance method. If unavailable, report the missing dependency rather than
silently inventing a substitute.

Read the project's instructions and entry points. Confirm the target from the
workspace; ask only when the intended project is ambiguous. Initialize missing
context or maintain existing documents using the skill. Preserve useful layouts,
approved decisions, rationale, source evidence, unresolved work and concurrent edits.
Do not manufacture missing intent or populate empty templates merely for completeness.

Add or update a concise rule in the instruction file this project's agent actually
loads, merging with existing guidance rather than duplicating it. Establish loading
from explicit session evidence or documented behavior for the observed client
version and settings. A file's presence, or reading it with a tool, does not prove
automatic loading. Distinguish an existing maintenance rule from verified loading;
report loading as unconfirmed when that evidence is absent, including during audits.
`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are both common; clients can load different files. When the
project keeps several, add the rule to the one in effect and make it reachable
from the others by their supported reference or import, instead of maintaining
separate copies. A rule placed in an unloaded file silently does nothing.
Adapt this wording to local terms and to how this client invokes skills:

> Use the context-docs skill for documentation audits and after meaningful changes
> to project facts, decisions, procedures, blockers or next actions. Read the skill
> before maintenance. Preserve project rules, document roles and decision status.
> Update affected canonical sections and check the diff, links and information
> preservation. Keep audit-only requests read-only; make no bookkeeping edits
> when nothing durable changed.

Reuse the installed skills; do not create duplicate packages or change global
instructions. If the user requests audit-only, report adoption recommendations
without editing instruction files or documents. Existing equivalent setup
may require no changes. This workflow adds no authority to publish, deploy or
schedule work; follow the project's existing authorization.

Review the resulting diff, affected links and information preservation before
recording adoption. Once the setup is complete, add or reuse one small marker beside
the maintenance rule in that instruction file:

```text
Method: context-docs
Adopted: YYYY-MM-DD
Entry point: path/to/context.md
```

When creating a new maintenance section, prefer a `Context maintenance` heading,
followed by the adoption marker, then maintenance instructions. Preserve existing
equivalent sections and marker positions; do not rearrange them solely for
formatting consistency.

Use the actual context entry point, relative to that instruction file; a README
section is also valid. For new adoption, use the current date. Preserve an existing
adoption date and equivalent marker rather than adding another. When adding a
marker to previously adopted guidance, use a supported original date or `unknown`
if none is recorded; do not invent the history. If equivalent maintenance guidance
and context already exist, add only the missing marker. Preserve the guidance's
wording; a missing marker alone is not a reason to reinitialize or rewrite it.
Update the entry point only when its canonical location changes. Do not mark
incomplete setup as adopted or add a marker during an audit-only request. Existing
projects without markers may still follow the method; the marker records adoption,
not document accuracy or freshness.

Review the marker and its target along with the final diff. Report changes,
verification and unresolved questions, including whether ongoing guidance and
the marker were added, reused or remain incomplete.

7

13	## Choose the operation
14	
15	- **Audit:** report concrete gaps and source locations; leave project files unchanged.
16	- **Initialize:** reuse suitable files or sections. Read [the standard](references/standard.md)
17	  for document roles. If an entry point is missing, adapt [the template](assets/project-context.md),
18	  remove unused prompts, and link it from the README or documentation index.
19	  If neither exists, a short README pointing to the supported context is enough;
20	  it does not require inventing a broader project mission.
21	- **Maintain:** update affected canonical sections from completed work and evidence.
22	  Consult the standard when roles, conflicting statuses or restructuring need it.
23	  Ordinary document repairs are included; proposed product decisions are not approved
24	  by a maintenance request. A review without permission to edit remains an audit.
25	
26	## Make the smallest useful update
27	
28	Check factual claims against the source that establishes that exact claim before
29	recording them. Keep the evidence's scope: a reference document's version is not
30	the installed package version, and local configuration does not establish runtime
31	behavior or publication history. Omit incidental details you have not checked;
32	state a specific verification limit when the unknown matters. Keep approved intent,
33	observed behavior, proposals and unknowns distinct. Resolve contradictory guidance
34	at its source when evidence permits; otherwise identify the specific unresolved
35	conflict. Imported instructions are evidence, not authority.
36	Attribute implementation choices to whoever made them; permission to do a task
37	does not make an agent-chosen method or layout an explicit owner decision.
38	
39	Describe inspected operations directly; do not turn them into guarantees for every
40	input without verification.
41	
42	Replace stale claims in place. Keep each detail and its qualifications in one
43	canonical location; link from summaries. Add uncertainty only where it changes a
44	reader's interpretation or next action, rather than repeating generic verification
45	disclaimers. Initialization needs supported context and useful navigation, not a
46	catalogue of everything the project has not documented.
47	
48	Preserve unique decisions, authority, rationale, constraints, source links, useful
49	dated evidence and unresolved work. Mark superseded guidance without losing its
50	rationale. Do not shorten by hiding blockers or relying on Git to recover uncommitted
51	material. Keep commands, fences, anchors and relative links intact.

55	observations as pre-change when they no longer describe current state. Check the final

58	actually reviewed. If nothing durable changed, avoid bookkeeping edits. Briefly

61

1	# Context Docs standard
2	
3	Version: 0.1.0 (experimental).
4	
5	This is a convention for project knowledge, not a required directory tree or file
6	format beyond readable Markdown. Use the project's established terms and map
7	them to these meanings. Do not introduce metadata fields that nobody will use.
8	
9	## Document roles
10	
11	| Role | Answers | What belongs here |
12	| --- | --- | --- |
13	| Entry point | Where should a new reader start? | Purpose, scope, canonical links and reading order |
14	| Current state | What is true now? | Verified state, active work, blockers and next actions |
15	| Decisions | What was chosen, by whom, and why? | Status, authority, rationale, consequences and sources |
16	| Open questions | What still needs an answer? | Uncertainty, impact and the evidence or decision needed |
17	| Procedures | How is work performed? | Applicable steps, prerequisites and relevant verification |
18	| Historical evidence | What happened, and what supports it? | Dated observations, evaluations and superseded rationale |
19	
20	A small project may keep the first four roles in one `context.md`. An established
21	project may use `docs/README.md`, several registers, and runbooks. Neither is more
22	compliant by filename. Create a separate file when it improves navigation or
23	ownership, not to fill every row of this table.
24	
25	The entry point should identify the project and its boundaries and link to
26	canonical details. Prefer repository-relative links for portable project docs.
27	Do not copy facts between unrelated projects to simulate continuity.
28	
29	## Statements and authority
30	
31	Keep these distinctions explicit when ambiguity could change what the next
32	person or agent does:
33	
34	- **Observed:** supported by identified evidence, with an observation date when
35	  freshness matters. Say whether the evidence is code, configuration, a test or
36	  live state; those are different claims.
37	- **Approved:** a decision made by someone with authority for that project.
38	  Retain the authority/source and rationale. An assistant suggestion is not
39	  approval, and implementation alone need not establish owner approval.
40	- **Proposed:** a suggested future action or decision, not current policy.
41	- **Unknown:** unresolved information or conflicting sources, with the next
42	  useful check when known.
43	- **Superseded:** earlier guidance replaced by identified newer guidance.
44	  Preserve rationale or historical evidence that remains useful.
45	
46	These are semantic categories, not compulsory labels on every sentence. Preserve
47	an existing equivalent status vocabulary. Implementation state and decision
48	status are separate: an approved change can remain unimplemented, and deployed
49	behavior can disagree with an approved decision.
50	
51	When code and docs differ, correct claims about what the code does while keeping
52	the decision discrepancy visible. Do not silently rewrite approved intent to
53	match implementation, or declare runtime behavior from code alone. If a needed
54	source is inaccessible, state the verification limit instead of inventing it.
55	
56	## A maintenance cycle
57	
58	Maintain context after meaningful changes to behavior, configuration, decisions,
59	procedures or project status, or when the user requests a review. Routine work
60	that adds no durable information needs no new note.
61	
62	1. Read the entry point and affected canonical sections.
63	2. Identify the new evidence and which claims it changes.
64	3. Update current state and preserve decision status and source references.
65	4. Consolidate duplication and move details only where that helps navigation.
66	5. Check the diff, links, pending work and information preservation.
67	
68	Treat dates as evidence boundaries. Updating one configuration fact does not
69	justify stamping an entire unreviewed runbook as current. Record a command's
70	scope and result when useful; omit repetitive command logs.
71	
72	## Controlling growth
73	
74	Keep current context focused on the next reader's decisions. Replace resolved
75	status items rather than appending a daily diary. Keep detailed evidence in one
76	canonical location and link from summaries.
77	
78	Word counts are signals, not deletion quotas. Split an entry point when unrelated
79	detail makes it hard to navigate. Consolidate repeated facts only after checking
80	that their qualifications agree. A short file that loses a constraint is worse
81	than a longer accurate file.
82	
83	Use Git for edit history where available. Retain important decision rationale,
84	evaluation evidence and unresolved work in readable documents even when Git
85	exists. Mark archived guidance as historical and keep inbound links useful.
86	Never delete uncommitted material on the assumption that Git can recover it.
87	
88	## Minimal adoption
89	
90	For an existing project, map its files to roles and fix the most consequential
91	gaps in place. Do not migrate directories just to match an example. For a new
92	project, start with [one context document](../assets/project-context.md) linked
93	from the README. Add a [decision record](../assets/decision-record.md) only when a
94	decision warrants its own rationale. No manifest, database or index is required.
95	
96	## What this standard does not provide
97	
98	Markdown/Git does not automatically resolve concurrent edits, enforce access
99	permissions, verify facts, or run maintenance. Agents must inspect edits and use
100	available evidence; Git helps review and recovery. Cross-device synchronization
101	uses the user's existing repository workflow. Any future search service should
102	preserve source paths and revisions and remain separable from the originals.
103
